acceptance.criterion: Instance, route, origin, connection, request, stream, and managed-buffer accounting follows real owners.
acceptance.evidence: A single per-client or per-server ledger is shared across protocol pools. Connection, request, stream, and buffer leases track origin/route ownership and release on their owning lifecycle. H1/H2 and ALPN handoffs retain physical connection ownership.

acceptance.criterion: Admission waits and queues are bounded; cancellation removes waiters; lease release is exact-once.
acceptance.evidence: Configured waiter ceilings, context-bound waits, cancellation/deadline waiter removal, owner-fair grants, and idempotent reference-counted leases are covered by focused regression tests. Server request/stream refusal is nonblocking.

acceptance.criterion: Snapshots expose current and lifetime high-water resource counts and bounded owner rows.
acceptance.evidence: Public client/server snapshots expose effective limits, current and high-water counters, and currently active origin/route owners. Facade tests inspect snapshots during H1/H2 activity and after shutdown/release.

acceptance.criterion: Managed HTTP/2 buffers share an aggregate budget with control-frame reserve and slow-I/O backpressure.
acceptance.evidence: Received DATA segments and queued/active serialized writer frames share the managed-byte ceiling; receive buffers are released on body consumption/close and writer reservations release on completion or cancellation. Documentation explicitly excludes RSS and unaccounted runtime/native/application memory.

acceptance.criterion: Defaults, hard caps, backpressure, and refusal behavior are documented; dependency boundaries remain valid.
acceptance.evidence: The HTTP/1.1 guide records client/server defaults, validation caps, cross-field receive-window rule, wait behavior, H1 503 and H2 REFUSED_STREAM behavior, and accounting scope. The architecture guard passes; public source inventory includes the new API file.
